article.headline: Storms and flooding set to drench Australia during wild weekend weather
article.summary: Severe weather warnings for heavy rain and flash flooding impact Tasmania as storms hit the Australian east and south-east coast this weekend.
article.body: Six-hourly rainfall totals are predicted to reach between 40mm and 70mm, bringing a significant risk of flash flooding to parts of northern Tasmania by early Saturday morning. This drenching rain is expected to push into the state from the north throughout Friday evening, spreading across the entire region overnight. The Bureau of Meteorology has confirmed that the weather system, fed by tropical moisture, creates an evolving risk for residents. Flood watches are currently in place for several key waterways, including the Forth, Mersey, Meander, North Esk, and Tamar rivers, as well as various north coastal rivers where sudden rises are deemed likely. The weekend forecast across the broader Australian landscape presents a sharp contrast in extremes. While parts of the east coast brace for these intense storms and potential floods, other regions are battling heatwaves and dangerous bushfires. On Flinders Island, an out-of-control fire has already destroyed or damaged at least eight buildings. Tasmania fire service officials noted that while some rain is moving toward the island late Friday, the heaviest falls are expected to bypass the fire-ravaged areas, providing little relief for those contending with the blaze. Authorities remain on high alert as the combination of wind, rain, and fire creates a volatile situation for the weekend. Residents are urged to monitor local warnings and official reports from the Bureau of Meteorology closely as the weather patterns shift across the country throughout the coming days.

article.headline: Lloyds Banking Group app and online services crash across the UK
article.summary: Millions of Lloyds Bank and Bank of Scotland customers lost access to their accounts following a major digital outage on Friday morning.
article.body: Digital access for 28 million customers across the Lloyds Banking Group evaporated on Friday morning as the company’s mobile app and internet banking systems suffered a widespread failure. Beginning around 10am, users across the UK encountered persistent error messages, finding themselves unable to complete transactions, check account balances, or navigate basic banking functions. According to The Independent, the outage also crippled services for Bank of Scotland, which operates under the same banking group umbrella. While the bank’s official status page claimed no scheduled work was underway, it did acknowledge that telephone banking wait times had grown longer than usual. For customers, the sudden loss of digital connectivity created immediate friction, as the systems designed to provide constant access to funds became unreachable. Despite advice from the bank to simply log out and sign back in, many users reported that such attempts failed to restore service. The bank acknowledged the widespread difficulty in an official error message, stating they were working to return systems to normal as quickly as possible. As of the latest reports, the bank has provided no official timeline for a full restoration of its digital infrastructure. Customers currently face the uncertainty of limited account management until the technical issues are fully resolved by the group's internal teams.

article.headline: Nearly 300,000 Canadians sign massive petition to oust U.S. Ambassador Pete Hoekstra
article.summary: The Canadian House of Commons received a petition demanding the expulsion of U.S. Ambassador Pete Hoekstra for allegedly undermining diplomatic relations.
article.body:
Nearly 290,000 Canadians signed the petition, which calls for the government to declare Ambassador Pete Hoekstra "persona non grata" and strip him of his diplomatic status. Launched by Calgary resident Leanne Walker in July, the initiative argues that Hoekstra has repeatedly breached diplomatic protocol by interfering in Canadian domestic politics and encouraging Alberta separatism.

This petition presents a significant challenge for Prime Minister Mark Carney’s administration, which is now legally required to provide a formal response. While Green Party MP Elizabeth May, who sponsored the document, expressed doubt that the government will actually expel the envoy, she noted that the massive public support could provide leverage for Canada during critical trade negotiations with the United States. She cited recent history, noting that Canada has previously expelled foreign diplomats for activities involving foreign interference or criminal involvement.

Hoekstra, 72, has drawn significant criticism for publicly labeling Canada the "51st state" and accusing Canadian officials of meddling in U.S. elections. The ambassador described his comments as a "term of endearment" and questioned why Canadians took offense. Meanwhile, the U.S. State Department acknowledged awareness of the petition but declined to offer further comment. The petition specifically alleges that the ambassador normalized rhetoric that threatens Canadian sovereignty, prompting widespread unease across the country.

The federal government is obligated to deliver an official response to the House of Commons within 45 days. Whether or not the administration takes action to remove the ambassador remains uncertain, as the government traditionally prioritizes maintaining trade relationships while navigating ongoing disputes over tariffs.

article.headline: Detroit Lions owner Martha Firestone Ford dies at 101 years old
article.summary: The longtime owner and chair emeritus of the Detroit Lions has passed away at her home surrounded by family.
article.body:
Martha Firestone Ford lived to the age of 101, closing a chapter on a life that included six decades of ownership of the Detroit Lions. She first became involved with the franchise in 1963 alongside her husband, William Clay Ford, before assuming sole control of the team following his passing in 2014.

Her leadership provided stability for the franchise and helped the team secure two playoff appearances in 2014 and 2016. Beyond the field, her tenure included significant financial investments in Ford Field, which the organization credits as the foundation for the current stadium experience. She was also a prominent figure in the Detroit community, notably launching the Detroit Lions Inspire Change initiative in 2019 and serving as a longtime trustee of Henry Ford Health.

Following her transition to the role of chair emeritus in 2020, Mrs. Ford supported her four children as they took on leadership responsibilities within the family franchise. The Green Bay Packers, longtime rivals of the Lions, released a statement expressing their sadness at the news and extended their condolences to the Ford and Firestone families.

Mrs. Ford’s legacy is carried forward by her children, including Sheila Ford Hamp, who currently serves as principal owner and chair. The Ford family continues to oversee the franchise, maintaining the traditions and values established during the couple's long tenure.

article.headline: Brooks Koepka and Justin Thomas headline $4 million Farmers Insurance Skins Game
article.summary: Four PGA Tour stars will compete for a $4 million prize at Atlantic Fields Golf Club on Black Friday.
article.body:
Four major champions and tour winners—Brooks Koepka, Wyndham Clark, Justin Thomas, and Jackson Koivun—are set to compete for a $4 million purse this Friday. The Farmers Insurance Skins Game returns for its second consecutive year, moving the action to the Atlantic Fields Golf Club in Hobe Sound, Florida. The event utilizes a classic format where each hole, or skin, carries a set dollar value, with tied holes resulting in a carry-over of the prize money. While traditional 72-hole tournaments demand intense focus, this made-for-TV competition allows the players to showcase their personalities in a more relaxed, conversational environment.

Fans gain unique access to the players through this format, as competitors are mic'd up throughout the day. This provides viewers with an opportunity to hear everything from lighthearted banter to the specific tactical discussions between golfers and their caddies. Wyndham Clark noted that he would welcome this increased level of transparency in standard tour events, comparing the potential experience to the style of production seen in NFL Films.

According to the PGA Tour, the event was originally meant to feature a press conference early in the week, but scheduling was shifted due to the extended conclusion of The RSM Classic. The delay provided a target for playful trash talk between the stars, with Koepka and Clark trading jokes about their absent competitor, Justin Thomas, and the inclusion of the rookie Koivun. 

The competition will be broadcast on Prime Video throughout the day on Friday. Amazon will host the golf coverage as part of a larger sports slate, which includes an NFL game between the Broncos and the Steelers, followed by NBA matchups in the evening. Access to the stream will be available without requiring a subscription or Prime membership.

article.headline: Jaguars receiver Parker Washington ruled out for Sunday with shoulder injury
article.summary: Jacksonville wide receiver Parker Washington will miss Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans due to a shoulder injury sustained in practice.
article.body:
Parker Washington sustained his shoulder injury during Thursday's practice session in Jacksonville, moving from off the injury report to being ruled out in less than 48 hours. The wide receiver was coming off a high-profile performance last Sunday against the New York Giants, where he recorded eight catches for 103 yards despite a controversial fourth-quarter ruling that denied him a touchdown pass. Head coach Liam Coen officially confirmed the injury status on Friday.

For the Jaguars, losing their primary receiving option poses a significant challenge for the upcoming game against the Titans. Washington has emerged as the team's top pass-catcher this season, leading the roster in every major receiving category with 44 total catches, 748 yards, and six touchdowns. His absence disrupts an offensive core already managing injuries to other key players, including running back Bhayshul Tuten.

According to reports from Sports Illustrated and NBC Sports, Washington's effectiveness has been critical to the Jaguars' passing attack, particularly on downfield targets where he has accounted for 483 receiving yards. While the team maintains depth with pass-catchers such as Jakobi Meyers, Brenton Strange, Brian Thomas Jr., and Josh Cameron, none function as a direct replacement for Washington's specific role in the slot.

Looking ahead, the coaching staff has designated Washington as a week-to-week player. The Jaguars continue to prepare for their Week 12 matchup against Tennessee without his availability, while the team balances the need for offensive continuity amidst a critical stretch of the season.

article.headline: Canada’s CRTC Orders Telecom Giants to Halt Prohibited Wireless Surcharge Fees
article.summary: The CRTC has directed Bell, Rogers, and Telus to eliminate prohibited activation and hardware-related fees by December 27.
article.body:
Bell sold cellphones locked to its network for up to 60 days, a practice the regulator determined breached the Wireless Code by restricting a customer's ability to switch service providers. The CRTC is now weighing a financial penalty of up to $10 million against Bell, marking an aggressive move toward the upper limit of enforcement options available under the Telecommunications Act.

For millions of Canadian mobile users, this ruling aims to dismantle a cycle of hidden charges that appeared shortly after a June ban on standard activation and cancellation fees. While the regulator is forcing the removal of these costs, customers who have already paid the surcharges will not receive automatic refunds; they must instead file complaints through the Commission for Complaints for Telecom-television Services to seek recourse.

According to the CRTC, the major carriers introduced specific hardware and SIM-related charges that essentially functioned as disguised activation fees despite previous prohibitions. Sean Carter, the CRTC’s acting vice president of consumer analytics and strategy, stated that the commission identified the prohibited fees and notified the companies, yet the providers chose to maintain them while arguing they were legal. The regulator has declared that if these companies fail to comply by the December 27 deadline, it will initiate immediate enforcement actions.

Beyond the fee crackdown, the regulator rejected a formal request from Telus to allow the locking of cellphones for 60 days following activation. Bell, which maintained that its locking policy was implemented to combat fraud and store theft, stated it is currently reviewing the CRTC’s decision. The commission has invited Bell to comment on the potential $10 million fine before a final ruling on that penalty is issued.

article.headline: Labor’s 12-year Victorian reign nears end as polls close on Saturday
article.summary: Victorian voters head to the polls on Saturday, November 28, to decide the state government as Labor's long-term leadership faces an expected defeat.
article.body:
Opposition Leader Jess Wilson is facing fierce opposition from One Nation’s Warren Pickering over a proposed $9.2 billion lease of Melbourne Water’s sewerage treatment plants, pipes, and pumping stations. This 90-year lease proposal represents a major point of contention heading into the final hours of the election campaign, with One Nation pledging to vote against the legislation required to enact such a deal. One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has been actively touring Melbourne’s northern and western suburbs to support her party's candidates as they seek to secure the balance of power in the upper house. Meanwhile, Premier Ben Carroll has cautioned against the influence of the populist party, suggesting the Opposition Leader will regret aligning with their political agenda. This dispute highlights the shifting political landscape as the state transitions away from the long-term Labor administration.

For voters, the election represents a critical choice between the outgoing government and a Coalition platform that includes plans to slash net debt and cut annual interest repayments. The decision to privatize critical infrastructure remains a flashpoint, reflecting deeper concerns about budget management and the state's fiscal future. Labor's 12-year period in power, led successively by Daniel Andrews, Jacinta Allan, and Ben Carroll, is widely expected by pollsters to conclude once the final votes are tallied.

Both major parties have traded barbs over fiscal policy and transparency. Wilson has criticized One Nation for failing to submit their policies to the Department of Treasury and Finance or the Parliamentary Budget Office for independent scrutiny. One Nation, conversely, claims it will rebuild the state budget from scratch while opposing the Coalition’s infrastructure leasing strategy. Voting centers are scheduled to close at 6pm on Saturday, November 28, marking the conclusion of the campaign cycle and the start of the transition to a new parliament.

article.headline: Australia Pips England By Three Wickets In Gripping T20 Series Opener
article.summary: Australia clinched a three-wicket win over England with one ball to spare in the first T20 match at the MCG.
article.body:
Jack Edwards drilled a boundary from Sam Curran’s penultimate delivery to seal a dramatic victory for Australia in front of a 39,000-strong crowd. The home side, fielding an unfamiliar lineup, successfully chased down England's record total of 187 for nine to claim the win with only one ball remaining in the contest. The result provides a lift for the home side following a difficult week for Australian cricket.

At the heart of the result was Nikhil Chaudhary, an India-born all-rounder who previously arrived in the country on a travel visa during the 2020 pandemic. Chaudhary claimed two wickets to stifle England’s batting momentum, including the crucial dismissal of Harry Brook, who had scored 65 from 28 deliveries. The all-rounder then anchored the response with a 38-ball 66 at number four, fundamentally breaking the back of the English bowling attack.

Despite the victory, the night brought injury concerns for the tourists. England vice-captain Will Jacks was forced to leave the field with a bleeding bowling hand after being struck by a powerful drive from Ben Dwarshuis. England, who recently recovered from a 1-0 deficit during their one-day series, now look toward the remaining fixtures in the five-match T20 tour.

Meanwhile, the second T20 match between the two sides has moved to Carrara, Queensland. During this second encounter, Australia’s Ben Dwarshuis showcased his athleticism by plucking a spectacular caught-and-bowled dismissal from a Phil Salt pull shot.
